_comment: Which pages of a design export get shipped, and under what name.
The export folder holds the same nine pages twice:
ever read these, and that script is retired (see below).
production/*.html    the bundled build, ~1.1 MB each, already named for
deployment. THIS is what build-live-pages.js reads --
it needs the manifest/template blocks the bundler emits.
So there is no rename to do: the design tool already emits deployed names.
What this file actually pins down is the ALLOW-LIST -- which of the nine
bundled pages ship. That matters because build-live-pages.js fails on any
page in its input that is not declared in PAGES, so pointing it at
production/ as-is dies on tracker-new.html every single time. The old fix was
to delete that file from the export by hand before each build.
Keys are filenames inside production/. Values must match PAGES in
'ignore' is not a junk drawer -- each entry carries its reason, because an
unexplained entry is indistinguishable from a page someone forgot to wire.

ignore.tracker-new.html: Superseded 'New Views' prototype, DELETED 2026-08. netlify.toml and public/staticwebapp.config.json both 301 /tracker-new to /tracker, and it is absent from PAGES, so build-live-pages.js would abort on it. dev/build-new-views.js (which built it from 'OLH Tracker - New Views.dc.html') is kept for history but is NOT part of the release path.
